input: Organize a charity auction for the school fundraiser

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The scale of the auction — number of items, live vs. silent vs. online format — completely changes the planning effort and coordination required.
Knowing who is organizing this (a parent committee, school staff, a single coordinator) determines how tasks are delegated and who owns each piece.
The event date and venue affect almost every downstream decision: booking, promotion timeline, and logistics.
The available budget for running the event (before fundraising revenue) sets hard limits on venue, tools, marketing, and staffing.
Having a specific fundraising target clarifies how many items are needed, what minimum bid levels to set, and whether the event was a success.
Whether bids will be managed on paper, with a dedicated app, or via an online platform determines the tools, training, and payment processing needed.
The intended audience (families, local businesses, community members) shapes how items are sourced, how the event is themed, and how it is marketed.

gold.taskTitle: Organize a School Charity Auction Fundraiser
gold.taskDescription: Plan and execute a charity auction event to raise funds for the school, covering everything from item sourcing to event logistics.

questions.title: Is this a live, silent, or online auction format?
questions.description: Clarify the auction format to determine the scale, structure, and complexity of the event plan.

questions.title: Who is leading and helping organize this event?
questions.description: Identify the organizing team — parent volunteers, school staff, or a single coordinator — to plan task delegation appropriately.

questions.title: When is the event and has a venue been chosen?
questions.description: Establish the target date and location to set the planning timeline and surface any booking or space constraints.

questions.title: What budget is available to run the event itself?
questions.description: Determine the operational budget (separate from money raised) to set limits on venue hire, tools, printed materials, and staffing.

questions.title: What is the fundraising goal you want to hit?
questions.description: Define the target amount to raise so item values, bid minimums, and the number of lots can be calibrated accordingly.

questions.title: How will bids be collected and payments processed?
questions.description: Decide whether bidding is managed on paper bid sheets, a mobile app, or an online platform to determine the tools and training needed.

questions.title: Who is the primary audience attending the auction?
questions.description: Identify whether attendees are mainly school families, local businesses, or the wider community to guide item sourcing, theming, and marketing.
